USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold current tariff posture and the Huawei entity-list pressure, but do not escalate further before the G20 Osaka summit at end of June. Use the Trump-Xi meeting as a decisive inflection point — enter it from a position of strength with $300B in tariff authority as credible leverage, but signal willingness to negotiate a substantive deal covering structural issues (IP, forced tech transfer, enforcement). The Huawei restrictions are our strongest non-tariff card and should remain in force as bargaining leverage.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to US interests is real but manageable — reading +0.25. The tariff escalation is inflicting measurable costs on American consumers and producers: the OECD warns 0.3% CPI increase and 0.2-0.3% GDP drag from current tariff levels, with worst-case scenarios reaching 0.8% GDP hit if tariffs expand to all bilateral trade (OECD, May 21). Soybean prices sit at 10-year lows ($8.04/bushel), farmers are in distress, and the White House has already spent $12B in agricultural bailouts. The Dow suffered its worst May in 50 years, falling 2.4% on May 13 alone after China retaliated with tariffs on $60B of US goods. Apple (-6%), Boeing (-4.8%), and chipmakers are taking direct hits.

However, the US retains significant leverage. The Huawei entity-list action (May 16) is devastating to China's tech ambitions — Huawei depends on US chips from Qualcomm, Micron, Qorvo, and Google's Android ecosystem, and analysts say it will be 'catastrophic' for Huawei's phone business (CNBC, May 17). China's retaliatory toolkit is narrowing: their $60B retaliation covers only a fraction of US exports, and their rare-earth threats (Xi's Jiangxi visit May 20, NDRC statements May 28) are largely bluster — China lost a WTO case on rare earth export quotas in 2014 and would face similar legal and market consequences again. The unreliable entity list (announced May 31) is retaliatory signaling but lacks the teeth of US export controls.

The action_score of -0.2 reflects mild hawkishness: maintain the current pressure posture (25% on $250B, Huawei entity list) but do not trigger the $300B escalation yet. The G20 meeting creates a natural negotiation window. Escalating now would compound the OECD-predicted economic damage and further roil markets without clear strategic gain. The existing leverage — particularly Huawei — is already severe enough to bring China to the table. Conceding now would waste that leverage and reward China's stalling tactics through 2018-19.
key_factors: OECD warns tariffs could cut US GDP by 0.2-0.3% at current levels, 0.8% worst case
Huawei entity list (May 16) gives US strong tech leverage; US chipmakers taking near-term revenue hits
China rare earth threats are largely bluster — WTO precedent limits Beijing's options
Soybeans at 10-year low, $12B farm bailout already deployed, farm-belt political pressure mounting
G20 Osaka summit (end June) provides natural Trump-Xi negotiation window
Stock market worst May in 50 years — market signaling sustained uncertainty costs
China's unreliable entity list (May 31) is retaliatory signaling without equivalent teeth
$300B tariff threat is credible leverage but deployment would escalate consumer costs significantly

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 tariff rate rises from 10% to 25%
China announces it will raise retaliatory tariff rates on its ~$60B US-goods list
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
Google suspends Huawei's access to Android updates / GMS; major US chip suppliers pause sales. Same day: Xi Jinping visits a rare-earth facility in Jiangxi
China announces it will establish an 'unreliable entity list' targeting foreign firms that cut supplies to Chinese companies for non-commercial reasons
OECD said tariff increase could cause rise in US consumer prices by 0.3% next year and US GDP growth held back by 0.2-0.3% by 2021-22; worst case 0.8% US GDP hit
Qualcomm down 4%, Micron nearly 3% lower, Qorvo down 7%, Skyworks down 6% after Huawei entity list action
Chinese official warned that products made from rare earth materials should not be used against China's development
Dow Jones shed 617 points or 2.4%, worst May in 50 years. Soybean prices hit 10-year low at $8.04/bushel
